purpose: Round-5 study slots (track 1), main job at 48 trajectories per half (fits a 40 GB card): slot encoders with memory on raw gliders level 0, 3000 steps, up to 14 configs in priority order (supervised capacity control, closure, warm start, reconstruction, local law, no k-means prior, classic slot AE)
notes: Replaces r5-slots-007, which FAILED on an A100_40GB ($1.04 billed): the references and sam_sup ran (9.4 s per 100 training steps, as on the H200; sam_sup 2000 steps in 264 s), then all 13 other configs died at their first validation after a training chunk with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED in jit_val (17-19 GiB) while only 17% of the BFC pool was in use (logs/train.log): the pool, capped at 36 GiB, could not supply a second contiguous block of that size (small arrays that outlive a call sit inside the one large region), and it could not grow. SAME code, same ref 7099a0ded; env changes only: XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=platform (every device allocation goes to CUDA directly and is released when freed, so no contiguous pool is needed; this workload makes few, large allocations, 100 training steps per call, so the per-allocation cost is negligible; the job fails within the first minute if this JAX build rejects the value) and S5_STEPS=3000 (the measured speed leaves room: about 450 s per config, all 14 configs and the references in about 1.9 h on this card). Memory with that allocator: resident data 5.2 GiB plus one call's temporaries at a time (17-19 GiB validation, about 22-25 GiB training chunk; at the failure the chunk's block was already free, so they do not overlap), about 27-30 GiB of 40. cap_usd 20.80 = what is left of the study's $25 ($3.13 + $1.04 billed); it covers an H100 offer up to $5.52/h at max_hours 3.5. Expected spend: about $4 on an A100_40GB at $1.99/h, about $9 on the H100 at $5.02/h. Limits as before (training stops at 10400 s, no new certification item after 11200 s, workers killed at 11900 s; the job ends early when the config list is done; no config starts with under 1000 s left before the training deadline). An error in one config is caught and the grid goes on (that is what happened in r5-slots-007: its 32 certified halves and sam_sup's outputs were written). 48 trajectories per half (the doubled data of the full size stays dropped so that the job fits a 40 GB card). No network or subprocess use outside setup; job.sh starts its own CPU certification workers.
